key_insight: A consensus-based multi-agent LLM pipeline can improve HTS code classification by combining retrieval, evidence-grounded reasoning, voting, and human oversight instead of relying on a single-shot prediction.
engineering_relevance: For smart ports and maritime logistics, the framework supports more accurate, auditable, and compliance-oriented tariff coding under ambiguous real-world product descriptions.
method: Multi-agent retrieval over official tariff documents and legal notes
Evidence-grounded reasoning with hierarchical, element-wise voting for HTS components
Confidence estimation with human-in-the-loop escalation for uncertain cases
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate on a private dataset of 3,300 expert-labeled product records and report that accuracy drops from chapter-level prediction to fine-grained 10-digit suffix assignment.
watch_item: Performance is still difficult at the exact 10-digit level, so deployment should preserve uncertainty handling and human review for low-confidence cases.
paper_title: Consensus-based Agentic Large Language Model Framework for Harmonized Tariff Schedule Code Classification
